Which AI consulting service do you need?

A strategy workshop, a data foundation and a working pilot are three different purchases. Start with the deliverable you need to accept.

Find a match for my project

Three AI consulting services to shortlist by deliverable

A finance director asking for an AI strategy and a support lead replacing an agent desktop can receive nearly identical proposals. Start with what your team needs to accept at the end of the engagement. These three cases give you different deliverables to put in a brief.

We chose these examples for the specific work documented in a client case or product guide. Client outcomes are provider-reported. AY Automate publishes this guide.

  1. Slalom · A contact-center rollout

    Slalom describes moving 180 Genie agents onto a new contact-center solution. That makes it a useful first interview for a support leader who owns routing, agent training and service continuity. Ask to see the release plan for the first queue and an example of an issue the operations team could fix after handover.

    Read the source from Slalom

  2. Capgemini · A shared automation service

    Capgemini describes establishing a global automation service with ZF. A buyer funding several teams can use that case to ask who decides which workflow gets built next. Request a backlog example with the estimated effort, business owner and sign-off for a completed automation.

    Read the source from Capgemini

  3. AY Automate · Document checks with exceptions

    AY Automate publishes a workforce compliance case involving document verification for festival crews. A coordinator buying a similar service should bring an expired document, an unreadable scan and a record that needs human review. Ask the team to show the outcome for all three before pricing a rollout.

    Read the source from AY Automate

What to ask before you buy

  1. For an assessment, ask for a prioritized backlog with an owner and a baseline for each opportunity.
  2. For a pilot, agree on a test dataset, an acceptance threshold and the decisions a human will retain.
  3. For a rollout, get a handover plan covering monitoring, recurring costs and incident response.

How to compare prices

Request separate prices for discovery, implementation and ongoing support. Compare the cost of the first accepted workflow and the monthly cost to keep it running.
